task: Timing-gate tooling only: make PAL frame overruns detectable and comparable between builds. No gameplay, enemy, renderer, raster, VBI/DLI, memory or projectile code changed; wait_frame_at_line is untouched.

wip.description: WIP 4.5d Enemy Identity Freeze - NOT a candidate

baseline.description: feat(bomber): place the 4.5c Bomber formation in HYBRID_C_ARENA

counter_limitation.claim: missed_frames and extra_vbi_boundaries cannot detect a PAL frame overrun.
counter_limitation.reason: Both are derived from Atari800_nframes boundaries crossed inside one traced main-loop iteration. A fighter-OPEN frame that arrives at publish_fighter_projectile_overlays too late simply parks in wait_frame_at_line until the same VCOUNT $77 comes round on the next physical frame. The iteration still crosses exactly one frame boundary, so the counters report 0.
counter_limitation.evidence: Both miss events measured below report missed_frames 0, extra_vbi_boundaries 0 and dli_sequence_violations 0 in the same rows whose wall cycles are 62,682 and 62,825.
counter_limitation.also_unreliable: Raw counts of rows over 31,200 or 32,568 conflate one real miss with its phase-shift aftermath (1,394 and 1,055 such rows for the two single miss events below) and must not be used to compare builds.

fence_model.synchronization_point: In fighter OPEN the main loop reaches profile_after_sector and calls publish_fighter_projectile_overlays, which does ldx #$77 / jsr wait_frame_at_line.
fence_model.window: wait_frame_at_line waits for VCOUNT == $77 and then for VCOUNT != $77. VCOUNT $77 covers PAL scanlines 238-239, so arrival anywhere inside those two scanlines still catches the fence and the wait exits on scanline 240.
fence_model.deadline: The start of scanline 240 of the row's own physical frame (frame base + 240 x 114 cycles). Arriving at or after it costs one whole PAL frame.
fence_model.first_model_rejected: An earlier version of this audit used the start of scanline 238 as the deadline. It produced a false positive at memory-integrity-xex-2-hunt-fire4 frame 1963 (margin -91, wall 26,781, 0 shifted-phase rows), which is a frame that arrived 91 cycles into scanline 238 and caught the fence normally.
fence_model.cross_check: The audit determines the overrun from profile_publication_begin (a caught fence releases at the window end, a missed one one physical frame later) and compares that against the arithmetic deadline. Across both full gate sets (132 replays, about 245,000 traced frames) the two agree on every row: fence_model_disagreements 0.
fence_model.capital_path: Capital frames take the other branch and do not use the $77 fence; they are bounded by wait_for_master_pal_frame, so their overrun test is wall_cycles > 35,568.
fence_model.phase_shift: After a miss the loop keeps starting one phase later (fighter row start moves from scanline 18 to ~250-273) until a new gameplay generation resyncs it. The audit derives the normal phase per replay and per publication path as the modal start scanline, and attributes shifted-phase overrun rows to the preceding miss event instead of counting new ones.

reports_per_replay: worst margin to the fence deadline
per miss event: row index, frame, host frame, wall cycles, pre-wait, margin, shifted-phase rows until resync
maximum wall cycles, rows over target and hard gate, shifted-phase rows
tool.wiring: scripts/runtime-wall-trace.mjs audits every traced replay inside the session loop and reports it immediately (so an unrelated later gate invariant cannot hide the evidence), writes build/runtime-wall-trace/pal-timing-audit.json, and sets a non-zero exit code on any distinct miss event.

gate_result.comparison_caveat: Replays diverge between the two builds once gameplay differs, so per-session margin deltas mix gameplay divergence with cost. The comparable figure is the distinct miss count and the worst margin across the whole gate set: 2 misses / -765 cycles on the WIP build against 0 misses / +781 cycles at 2a8ff26.

runs_per_build: node scripts/runtime-wall-trace.mjs (default full set, boot smoke included)
the sessions after the pre-existing abort, one --only-session run each
pre_existing_failures_identical_on_both_: weapon-pickup-contact-2-hunt-fire4: 'changed GTIA priority or the single erase/draw lifecycle' aborts the default run (already recorded in STATUS)
capital-muzzle-ring-2-sweep-fire4: 'observed a stale muzzle/flash code or invalid derived pointer'
capital-contact-allied-medium, capital-contact-hostile-medium, lower-playfield-hostile-contact-xex-hard: emulator exits with status 2
gate_coverage.note: None of these is caused by the audit; each behaves identically at 7b50bd6 and 2a8ff26. Their traces were audited where a CSV exists; the three status-2 sessions produce none.
